translation_en: Yahya ibn Habib narrated to me: Khalid—Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us: Sa‘id narrated to us, from Qatadah, with this chain and a similar report.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us. Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aishah, who said: Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas and Abd ibn Zam‘ah disputed over a boy. Sa‘d said, “Messenger of Allah, this is my brother’s son, Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. He entrusted him to me, saying that he was his son. Look at how much he resembles him.” Abd ibn Zam‘ah said, “This is my brother, Messenger of Allah. He was born in my father’s bed by his slave woman.” The Messenger of Allah looked at the boy and saw a clear resemblance to Utbah. He said, “He is yours, Abd. The child belongs to the marital bed, and the adulterer gets the stone. And veil yourself from him, Sawdah bint Zam‘ah.” She said: He never saw Sawdah again. Muhammad ibn Rumh did not mention the words “O Abd.”

Sa‘id ibn Mansur, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: They said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us. Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us. Both reported from al-Zuhri with this chain and a similar report, except that Ma‘mar and Ibn Uyaynah said in their reports, “The child belongs to the marital bed,” and did not mention, “The adulterer gets the stone.”

Muhammad ibn Rafi and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me. Ibn Rafi said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said, “The child belongs to the marital bed, and the adulterer gets the stone.”

Sa‘id ibn Mansur, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Abd al-A‘la ibn Hammad, and Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: They said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri. Ibn Mansur said: From Sa‘id, from Abu Hurayrah. Abd al-A‘la said: From Abu Salamah, or from Sa‘id, from Abu Hurayrah. Zuhayr said: From Sa‘id or Abu Salamah, one of them or both, from Abu Hurayrah. Amr said: Sufyan narrated to us, once from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id and Abu Salamah; once from Sa‘id or Abu Salamah; and once from Sa‘id, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report like Ma‘mar’s.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Rumh said: al-Layth informed us. Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah came to me joyful, his face beaming, and said, “Did you see that Mujazziz looked just now at Zayd ibn Harithah and Usamah ibn Zayd and said, ‘Some of these feet belong to one another’?”

Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to me; these are Amr’s words. They said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, who said: One day the Messenger of Allah came to me joyful and said, “Aishah, did you see that Mujazziz al-Mudliji came to me, saw Usamah and Zayd with a cloak covering their heads while their feet were visible, and said, ‘These feet belong to one another’?”

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated this to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, who said: A physiognomist came in while the Messenger of Allah was present and Usamah ibn Zayd and Zayd ibn Harithah were lying down. He said, “These feet belong to one another.” The Prophet was pleased by that and liked it, and he told Aishah.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me. Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar and Ibn Jurayj informed us. All of them reported from al-Zuhri with this chain and a similar meaning. Yunus’s report adds: Mujazziz was a physiognomist.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Hatim, and Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; these are Abu Bakr’s words. They said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, from his father, from Umm Salamah, that when the Messenger of Allah married Umm Salamah, he stayed with her for three nights and said, “You are not of little worth to your family. If you wish, I will stay with you for seven nights; if I stay with you for seven, I will stay seven with my other wives as well.”

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, that when the Messenger of Allah married Umm Salamah and she came to live with him, he said to her, “You are not of little worth to your family. If you wish, I will stay with you for seven nights; if you wish, I will stay for three, then make the rounds.” She said, “Stay for three.”

Abdullah ibn Maslamah al-Qa‘nabi narrated to us: Sulayman—Ibn Bilal—narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Bakr, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman, that when the Messenger of Allah married Umm Salamah and entered upon her, he intended to leave, but she took hold of his garment. The Messenger of Allah said, “If you wish, I will add to your time, but I will count it accordingly: a previously unmarried woman receives seven nights, and a previously married woman receives three.”
Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Damrah informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd, with this chain and a similar report.

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-Ala, narrated to me: Hafs—Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, from Umm Salamah. He mentioned that the Prophet married her and related some details of this account. It includes his saying, “If you wish, I will stay with you for seven nights, and if I stay with you for seven, I will stay seven with my other wives too.”

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When a man married a previously unmarried woman while already married to a previously married woman, he would stay with the new wife for seven nights; when he married a previously married woman while already married to a previously unmarried woman, he would stay with her for three nights. Khalid said, “If I said he attributed it to the Prophet, I would be telling the truth, but he said, ‘That is the practice.’”

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Sufyan informed us, from Ayyub and Khalid al-Hadhdha, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said: “It is the practice to stay with a previously unmarried wife for seven nights.” Khalid said, “If I wished, I could say he attributed it to the Prophet.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Prophet had nine wives. When he divided his time among them, he would not return to the first wife until nine days had passed. They would gather each night in the house of the wife he was visiting. He was at Aishah’s house when Zaynab came, and he reached out his hand toward her. She said, “This is Zaynab.” The Prophet withdrew his hand. They spoke sharply to one another until their voices rose. The prayer was called. Abu Bakr passed by, heard their voices, and said, “Come out to prayer, Messenger of Allah, and throw dust into their mouths.” The Prophet went out. Aishah said, “Now the Prophet will finish his prayer, then Abu Bakr will come and do such-and-such to me.” When the Prophet finished praying, Abu Bakr came to her, spoke sternly to her, and said, “Would you do this?”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, who said: I never saw a woman I would have liked more to be in her place than Sawdah bint Zam‘ah. She was a sharp-tempered woman. When she grew old, she gave her day with the Messenger of Allah to Aishah and said, “Messenger of Allah, I give my day with you to Aishah.” The Messenger of Allah then allotted Aishah two days: her own day and Sawdah’s day.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Uqbah ibn Khalid narrated to us. Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: al-Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us. Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Sharik narrated to us. All of them reported from Hisham with this chain that Sawdah had grown old, with the meaning of Jarir’s hadith. Sharik’s report adds that she said: She was the first woman he married after me.

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-Ala, narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, who said: I used to feel jealous of the women who offered themselves to the Messenger of Allah and would say, “Would a woman offer herself?” When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed, “You may defer whomever of them you will and receive to yourself whomever you will, and whoever you desire of those you have set aside…” Quran 33:51, I said, “By Allah, I see that your Lord hastens to fulfill your wishes.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated this to us: Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, who used to say: “Would a woman not feel ashamed to offer herself to a man?” Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed, “You may defer whomever of them you will and receive to yourself whomever you will” Quran 33:51. I said, “Indeed, your Lord hastens to fulfill your wishes.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us. Muhammad ibn Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Ata informed me: We attended the funeral of Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, with Ibn Abbas at Sarif. Ibn Abbas said, “This is the wife of the Prophet. When you lift her bier, do not jostle or shake it; be gentle. The Messenger of Allah had nine wives and divided his time among eight, not one.” Ata said: The one for whom he did not divide his time was Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab.
Muhammad ibn Rafi and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ibn Jurayj, with this chain. It adds: Ata said, “She was the last of them to die; she died in Medina.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ubaydullah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: They said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from Ubaydullah: Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id informed me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said, “A woman is married for four things: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty, and her religion. So choose the one with religion, may your hands be rubbed with dust.”
Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abd ibn Humayd narrated this to me, both from Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d, from Ibn Akhi al-Zuhri, from his uncle, with this chain and exactly the same report.

Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us; these are Ibn Abi Umar’s words. They said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “Woman was created from a rib, and she will not remain straight for you in one way. If you enjoy her, you enjoy her while she is crooked; if you try to straighten her, you will break her, and breaking her is divorcing her.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Husayn ibn Ali narrated to us, from Za’idah, from Maysarah, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said, “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, when he witnesses something let him speak good or remain silent. Treat women well, for woman was created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is its uppermost part. If you try to straighten it, you will break it; if you leave it, it will remain crooked. So treat women well.”

Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to me: Isa—Ibn Yunus—narrated to us: Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja‘far narrated to us, from Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Umar ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “A believing man should not hate a believing woman. If he dislikes one of her traits, he will be pleased with another.” Or he said, “another trait.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Asim narrated to us: Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Imran ibn Abi Anas narrated to us, from Umar ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a similar report.

Harun ibn Ma‘ruf narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Abu Yunus, the freedman of Abu Hurayrah, narrated to him, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said, “Were it not for Eve, no female would ever betray her husband.”
